prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you ate a salad at a barbecue. Respond to the committee.
response:
*rises, adjusts tie, places hand solemnly on a well-worn copy of the Weber Grill Owner's Manual*

Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the Committee, I come before you today of my own free will to clear my good name.

I want to state, unequivocally and for the record: I am not now, nor have I ever been, a salad eater at a barbecue.

The photograph in question — Exhibit A, which the Committee has circulated so recklessly — shows me holding a plate containing leafy green material. I do not deny this. But context, Mr. Chairman, context! That was *coleslaw*. Coleslaw, as this body well knows, is a constitutionally protected barbecue side dish, mayonnaise-based, and fully in keeping with American values.

Furthermore, the "lettuce" visible on my plate was serving in its proper patriotic capacity: as a *bed* beneath a pulled pork sandwich. It was structural, Mr. Chairman. Ornamental. I did not chew it. I did not enjoy it. I did not inhale.

Now, will I name names? *long pause, wipes brow*

...I saw Gerald from Accounting eating a quinoa cup. Near the horseshoe pit. He asked if the brisket was "grass-fed." I've said too much.

I close with this: I have consumed no fewer than four hot dogs, two burgers, and a rack of ribs at every cookout I have attended since 1994. My condiment record is spotless. I bleed barbecue sauce, Mr. Chairman.

May God bless this Committee, and may God bless the Grill.

*sits down, visibly sweating, loosens napkin tucked into collar*
